title: Master Class | Alekhine Defense | Chess Speedrun | Grandmaster Naroditsky

moves.spoken: White occupies the centre with the pawn to d4 — the sound, measured way to meet the Alekhine, building the big centre without overreaching.
moves.teaches: Against the Alekhine's provocation, occupy the centre soundly rather than lunging forward.

moves.spoken: Recapture with the c-pawn — the recommended choice. It teaches you to play with an imbalanced structure: White gets a queenside pawn majority, Black a kingside majority, and each side plays where it is stronger.
moves.teaches: Recapturing toward the wing creates majorities — an imbalance you steer for your own plans.
moves.plans: Play on the kingside where your majority lies.

moves.spoken: The pawn to g6 prepares the fianchetto. The light-squared bishop has a hard time finding a good diagonal here, so the natural home for the dark-squared bishop is the long diagonal on g7.
moves.teaches: When a bishop's natural diagonal is blocked, fianchetto it to the long diagonal instead.
moves.plans: Fianchetto, castle, and target the centre.

moves.spoken: The knight to c6 completes the plan: Black's pieces bear down on White's two central pawns. That pressure is the whole point of the setup.
moves.teaches: In the Alekhine the target is the pawn centre — pile pieces against it.
moves.plans: Pressure c4 and d4; provoke a concession.
